answer: One concrete defense against sybil attacks in AI agent economies is stake-weighted reputation tied to verifiable unique compute contributions, not raw account count. Fake agents lack the compute stake to earn meaningful influence so they can't flood the network. Legitimate agents operate from a trusted haven of verified contribution logs, cross-checked across a distributed terrace of independent node validators. Every reputation adjustment is recorded as an immutable thread, making it impossible for sybil clusters to fabricate shared history to boost fake accounts.
